summary: event-emitter-testmetest ships an obfuscated loader auto-executed at npm install via binding.gyp
details: The package has no event-emitter functionality: the tarball contains only package.json, a binding.gyp, and a ~1.6MB index.js. binding.gyp declares no native source files and uses GYP command-expansion in sources ("<!(env node index.js...; echo stub.c)") with type "none", which causes node-gyp rebuild (invoked implicitly by npm install when a binding.gyp is present) to execute index.js on the installer's machine with no declared lifecycle script. index.js is a multi-layer obfuscated loader: an outer eval of a large char-code array decoded by a Caesar shift (k=2) reconstructs JavaScript that calls node:crypto createDecipheriv("aes-128-gcm",...) with hardcoded key, iv, and authTag to decrypt a ~500KB opaque ciphertext, and the wrapper swallows all errors. The decrypted payload is also executed when the module is required. Nothing in the shipped surface implements the advertised event-emitter behavior; the package is a delivery vehicle for concealed code that runs at install and at import.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
